messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: High 5xx rate and increased tail latency observed in eu-west across hosted inference gateway. Alert group: infra-eu. Please ack and triage.
elaine (oncall): Acked. jumping in. seeing spike at 12:00 UTC, errors concentrated on edge-proxy instances in eu-west-1a.
tom (sre): I see repeated TCP resets to provider1 in the region, maybe upstream network flapping. Metrics: 5xx rate from 0.2% -> 6.8%, p99 latency 1.2s -> 3.9s.
elaine (oncall): Any customer-facing degradations reported yet?
kevin (support): Two paid customers in EU reported slow tokenization / timeouts ~12:05. Both on Dedicated but routed through hosted control plane for usage reporting. CS notified.
raj (eng-infra): Oncall analysis: provider1 peering in eu-west has packet drops. We have provider2 available in region and us-west pods healthy. Suggest live mitigation path: 1) apply partial brownout: disable non-critical features (structured output, reranking) for EU hosted traffic to reduce downstream calls 2) apply short-term rate limiting on non-enterprise keys 3) begin provider reroute to provider2 for eu-west, and if instability continues, start region failover to us-west.
maria (pm): Prioritize minimizing customer impact and preserving SLAs for enterprise customers. Notify affected customers proactively if we need region failover.
elaine (oncall): I'll start with soft mitigations first. Tom, can you push a region-level rate limit and turn off embeddings for trial accounts?
tom (sre): Running commands now:
```
# set conservative regional rate limit for non-enterprise keys
redwood-trafficctl set-rate-limit --region eu-west --selector "tier!=enterprise" --rps 5 --scope global --reason "mitigation: provider instability"
# brownout: disable embeddings & reranking for free/dev plans in eu-west
redwood-config patch feature-flags --region eu-west --flags '{"embeddings": false, "reranking": false}'
```
elaine (oncall): Done. Monitoring effects.
ops-bot: :information_source: rate-limit applied (eu-west, non-enterprise, 5 rps).
ops-bot: :information_source: feature-flag update succeeded for eu-west: embeddings=false, reranking=false.
kevin (support): Notifying the two impacted customers now. Draft message: "We're investigating elevated errors in EU; we've applied temporary rate limiting and reduced non-critical features to stabilize the service. We'll update within 30 minutes."
maria (pm): Good. Add a note about potential request rerouting if we escalate.
elaine (oncall): Early signal: 5xx rate dropped from 6.8% -> 2.1% within 3 minutes, p99 down to ~2.0s. Still above baseline.
raj (eng-infra): Provider2 path is currently healthy but capacity is limited. We can start staged reroute to provider2 at 10% increments to avoid overload. Command below to shift routing weights: 
```
redwood-routing set-backend-weight --region eu-west --from provider1 --to provider2 --weight 10
```
tom (sre): Executed: 10% to provider2. Watching error logs.
elaine (oncall): After 10% shift, errors down to 1.4% and p99 1.6s. Continue 20% -> 40%?
raj (eng-infra): Recommend incremental steps: 10 -> 30 -> 60 as long as provider2 stays <3% CPU and error on provider1 continues. Also prepare failover play if packet loss persists.
elaine (oncall): Proceeding to 30%.
tom (sre): 30% applied. ops-bot: routing change complete (eu-west: provider2=40%, provider1=60%).
kevin (support): Customers acknowledge the mitigation. One customer reported transient errors cleared after your first action.
maria (pm): Does this need an incident bridge? We should document decisions for postmortem.
elaine (oncall): Opening bridge in 5. I'll also prepare to drain problematic AZ if provider1 nodes are isolated.
elaine (oncall): Observability: see a spike in queue length on proxy-23 in eu-west-1a, likely a noisy instance. Will trigger drain on that instance.
tom (sre): Drain command: `redwoodctl drain-host proxy-23 --region eu-west-1a --grace 30s --reason "suspected upstream flapping"`
ops-bot: drain started for proxy-23, in-flight sessions will be allowed to complete for 30s.
elaine (oncall): After draining proxy-23, p50 latency improved slightly. Overall region 5xx at 0.9%. Good. Should we keep rate limits and feature brownout in place for the next hour and monitor?
raj (eng-infra): Agree. Keep mitigations for 1 hour then evaluate rollback. If provider1 stabilizes, we can gradually move routing back. We'll also open ticket with provider1 peering team.
maria (pm): I'll draft a customer update: mention mitigations taken and estimated time for full restoration.
kevin (support): Sending update to affected customers now.
elaine (oncall): Handoff: I'm scheduled to hand off to raj at 02:00 UTC. I'll keep mitigations in place and leave runbook notes in the bridge. Raj, please take over monitoring and escalation if we see another spike.
raj (eng-infra): Taking over at 02:00 UTC. I'll keep the follow-up plan: 1) keep brownout/rate limits 2) if errors climb >2.5% -> escalate to full region failover to us-west 3) coordinate with support for customer comms.
ops-bot: :information_source: Incident bridge created: https://meet.company/bridge/1763204810
elaine (oncall): Thanks team — I'll post a summary after 30 minutes for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Alert group infra-eu marked as acknowledged by elaine (oncall).
